title: ERRORRADAR: Benchmarking Complex Mathematical Reasoning of Multimodal Large Language Models via Error Detection
extended_summary:
This paper introduces ERRORRADAR, a new benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on mathematical error detection rather than standard problem solving. The authors argue that existing math benchmarks mostly assess whether models can solve problems correctly, but educational use cases require a more student-centered capability: identifying the first incorrect step in a solution and classifying the type of error made.

The benchmark consists of 2,500 multimodal K-12 mathematics problems collected from a global educational organization’s question bank and enriched with real student incorrect answers and step-by-step annotations. The data were manually annotated by professional educational experts to label the first erroneous step and one of five error categories: visual perception, calculation, reasoning, knowledge, and misinterpretation. The paper evaluates a range of open-source and closed-source MLLMs, along with human educators as a comparison standard, using the benchmark’s error-step identification and error-categorization tasks.

The population represented in the benchmark is K-12 students, though the paper does not specify grade-level breakdowns within K-12. The user roles present are students, whose incorrect work supplies the core data, and educators, who annotate and evaluate the responses. The paper is not an intervention study in a classroom setting; it is a benchmark and model-evaluation paper.

The main conclusion is that current MLLMs still struggle substantially with complex mathematical error detection. Closed-source models, especially GPT-4o, outperform open-source systems, but even the best models remain below human educator performance. The authors also find that identifying the erroneous step is easier than categorizing the error, calculation errors are easiest while knowledge errors are hardest, and model performance improves with scale mainly for step identification rather than error categorization.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-family multimodal large language model/chatbot used for general-purpose reasoning, text generation, and visual-language tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as one of several closed-source multimodal large language models on the ERRORRADAR benchmark for mathematical error detection in K-12 multimodal problems.

findings.finding_summary: GPT-4o was the strongest-performing model overall on ERRORRADAR, achieving 55.1% accuracy on error-step identification (STEP) and 53.1% on error categorization (CATE). It also obtained the highest category scores among MLLMs for visual perception (46.3%), reasoning (64.9%), and misinterpretation (46.3%).
findings.measure: Accuracy on error-step identification, error categorization, and per-error-category classification

identified_tools.name: Claude
identified_tools.description: Anthropic's Claude family of multimodal large language models/chatbots.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as a closed-source multimodal large language model on ERRORRADAR for detecting student math solution errors.

findings.finding_summary: Claude-3.5-Sonnet achieved 50.2% on STEP and 49.5% on CATE. Its category performance varied, with 35.7% on VIS, 48.4% on CAL, 64.8% on REAS, 21.0% on KNOW, and 11.4% on MIS.
findings.measure: Accuracy on error-step identification, error categorization, and per-error-category classification

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: Google's Gemini family of multimodal large language models/chatbots.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as a closed-source multimodal large language model on ERRORRADAR for error detection in K-12 math problem solving.

findings.finding_summary: Gemini-Pro-1.5 achieved 55.0% accuracy on STEP and 52.7% on CATE, ranking second on STEP among the closed-source models reported. Category accuracies were 43.5% (VIS), 55.7% (CAL), 63.1% (REAS), 18.5% (KNOW), and 13.0% (MIS).
findings.measure: Accuracy on error-step identification, error categorization, and per-error-category classification

identified_tools.name: Qwen
identified_tools.description: Alibaba's Qwen family of multimodal large language models/chatbots.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as both open-source and closed-source Qwen-VL variants on ERRORRADAR for student error detection.

findings.finding_summary: Qwen-VL achieved 23.8% on STEP and 38.9% on CATE, while Qwen-VL-Max achieved 48.7% on STEP and 52.9% on CATE. The closed-source Max variant also scored 15.2% (VIS), 78.9% (CAL), 50.5% (REAS), 14.3% (KNOW), and 36.6% (MIS).
findings.measure: Accuracy on error-step identification, error categorization, and per-error-category classification

identified_tools.name: LLaMA
identified_tools.description: Meta's LLaMA family of open-weight large language models used as the language backbone in several multimodal systems.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as the LLM backbone for several open-source multimodal models on ERRORRADAR, including LLaVA-v1.6-Vicuna and CogVLM2-LLaMA3, to assess error detection performance.

findings.finding_summary: As instantiated in open-source multimodal systems, performance varied: LLaVA-v1.6-Vicuna (Vicuna-v1.5 back end) scored 30.3% on STEP and 17.7% on CATE, while CogVLM2-LLaMA3 scored 15.0% on STEP and 20.1% on CATE. The paper reports strong category-specific differences across these LLaMA-based multimodal models, with especially low performance on KNOW for CogVLM2-LLaMA3 (0.7%).
findings.measure: Accuracy on error-step identification, error categorization, and per-error-category classification

identified_tools.name: DeepSeek
identified_tools.description: DeepSeek's multimodal large language model family.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as an open-source multimodal model (DeepSeek-VL) on ERRORRADAR for mathematical error detection.

findings.finding_summary: DeepSeek-VL scored 16.2% on STEP and 35.7% on CATE. Its category accuracies were 4.6% (VIS), 90.9% (CAL), 0.4% (REAS), 28.6% (KNOW), and 6.5% (MIS), showing particularly strong bias toward CAL classification.
findings.measure: Accuracy on error-step identification, error categorization, and per-error-category classification

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI or multimodal large language models with no single standalone student-facing product studied; the paper benchmarks multiple MLLMs on an error-detection task.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper benchmarks a collection of open-source and closed-source multimodal LLMs on a K-12 math error-detection benchmark rather than studying one instructional product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark paper, not a controlled intervention study in K-12 instruction. It reports model accuracies on a custom dataset, but does not evaluate educational outcomes from classroom use or compare to a non-AI instructional condition.
impact_tier_rationale: The work has clear technical relevance for educational AI evaluation and uses real K-12 student data, but it measures benchmark performance rather than instructional impact. The reported gains are model-accuracy differences without an educational treatment effect size.
